title: Breast Cancer Risk Assessment
description: Answer the following questions honestly to help estimate your personal risk factors for breast cancer. This assessment is based on widely recognised medical risk factors.
disclaimer: ⚠️ This quiz is for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Please consult a qualified healthcare professional for personalised guidance and diagnosis.

questions.question: Do you have a first-degree relative (mother, sister, daughter) diagnosed with breast cancer?
Have you ever been personally diagnosed with breast cancer, DCIS, or LCIS?
Have you undergone genetic testing that showed a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation?
At what age did you have your first menstrual period?
Have you gone through menopause? If yes, at what age?
Have you ever given birth to a child?
Have you used hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for more than 5 years?
How would you describe your alcohol consumption?
How would you describe your physical activity level?

options.text: Active (150+ minutes moderate exercise per week)

questions.question: What is your body weight status?
Do you smoke or have you smoked regularly in the past?

scoring.description: Your responses suggest a relatively low level of risk factors for breast cancer. Continue healthy habits and attend routine screenings as recommended for your age.
recommendations: Maintain a healthy weight and stay physically active.
Follow your doctor's advice on routine breast screening.

scoring.description: Your responses indicate a moderate level of risk factors. Awareness and proactive screening are especially important for you.
recommendations: Discuss your risk factors with your doctor.
Ensure you are up-to-date with recommended breast cancer screenings.
Consider lifestyle changes such as reducing alcohol intake and increasing physical activity.

scoring.description: Your responses suggest a higher level of risk factors for breast cancer. It is important to speak with a healthcare professional soon.
recommendations: Schedule an appointment with your doctor or a specialist as soon as possible.
Ask about enhanced screening options such as MRI in addition to mammography.
Discuss genetic counselling if you have a strong family history.
Make healthy lifestyle changes — diet, exercise, and reducing alcohol can all help lower risk.
Perform monthly breast self-examinations and report any changes immediately.

scoring.description: Your responses indicate a very high level of known risk factors. Urgent medical consultation is strongly advised.
recommendations: Consult a healthcare professional or oncologist promptly.
Request a comprehensive risk assessment and personalised screening plan.
Consider genetic testing for BRCA mutations if not already done.
Explore risk-reduction strategies including medication (chemoprevention) or preventive surgery if recommended by your doctor.
Build a strong support network and stay informed.
